text:
Alex Ribeiro: Heads up — we've started seeing intermittent OOMs on gpu-node-g6 when running the 16k chat workload with the new kernel selector. Root cause looks like combined effect of workspace spike + prefix cache shard flooding.
Maya Chen: repro steps?
Alex Ribeiro: small repro: run loadtest `./run_load.sh --model redwood-*,seq=16k --concurrency 48` for ~30m. OOMs show in kube logs then oom-bot posts:
oom-bot: [ALERT] gpu-node-g6: OOM triggered, process=redwood-runtime, pid=4821, rss=24.7G, alloc_request=512MB
Samir Patel: thanks. attaching profiler snippet from 2112345690 (warm):
```
kernel_selector: chosen=cu_attn_v2 (64B head optim), fallback=cu_attn_v1
workspace_allocator: pool_total=28G, in_use=22.3G, fragments=3.1G (11%), peak_request=4.2G
kv_prefix_cache: shards=6, entries=1.4M, mem=9.8G, eviction_rate=0.9/s
perf: p95=182ms, p99=460ms, tokens/s=120k
```
Maya Chen: kv_prefix_cache mem 9.8G + workspace 22.3G ~ 32.1G which exceeds node 32G (we have swap disabled). Are shards hot?
Zayd Noor: we saw hot shard skew on that workload — one shard had 40% of hits. TTL 10m currently.
Alex Ribeiro: proposal: 1) change kernel selector threshold to prefer cu_attn_v1 for seq>12k for specific params (reduces workspace per-kernel by ~800MB), 2) autoshrink prefix cache on kernel memory pressure (cooperative eviction), 3) raise workspace pool soft-limit and enable buffer reuse across kernels.
Eva Gomez: sounds good. Any metrics on regression risk if we force cu_attn_v1?
Samir Patel: quick A/B: cu_attn_v1 increases avg token latency by ~6% on small seq (<2k) but reduces p99 for long seq by 18% due to fewer OOM-driven retries. We need targeted rule: route seq>=12k to cu_attn_v1.
Maya Chen: cooperative eviction = if allocator reports fragmentation > 15% or free < 2G, trigger per-shard TTL reduce from 10m->60s and aggressive LRU until mem drops below threshold?
Zayd Noor: I ran a sim overnight: reducing TTL to 60s reduces cache memory ~65% and hit-rate drops from 0.78->0.56 for the 16k workload. But overall tokens/s improved because OOMs went away.
Alex Ribeiro: tradeoff accepted for bursty long-seq traffic; for stable workloads we keep default. Add fallback: if hit-rate falls <0.4 -> increase TTL back + spin up extra node.
Samir Patel: also one low-effort mitigator: enable workspace buffer recycling across kernels to reclaim ~1.2G steady-state. Patch ready in PR #4821.
Maya Chen: can we add a runtime gauge for "cooperative_eviction_active" and an annotation in traces when kernel_selector downgraded? Helps debugging later.
Alex Ribeiro: agreed. Also want an experiment: rollout to canary fleet (5% cap) with metrics: OOM count, p99, tokens/s, cache_mem, workspace_frag. If OOMs drop and p99 improves for long seq -> promote.
Eva Gomez: I'll own the canary and dashboards. ETA tomorrow EOD for dashboards.
Zayd Noor: quick note — be careful with shard count change during active runs. Re-sharding can spike allocations. Prefer TTL-based shrink first.
Samir Patel: ack. I'll open a playbook snippet for oncall: steps to revert kernel selector and how to reduce concurrency.
Alex Ribeiro: thanks all. I'll post PR links and the canary plan in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
